habitat: On the ground in bushveld savanna, from near sea level to about 2000 m on the eastern plateau. SABAP1 says it is mostly single and becomes moderately gregarious in the non-breeding season.
summary: No Newman page. Wikipedia gives dry forest and dry savanna and no plumage. SABAP1 says it has few salient features, is larger and longer-tailed than the Short-tailed Pipit, and has a characteristic call that is not described. No length, plumage or status is stored. The Kemp code RB was left unchanged.

calls.description: Neither Wikipedia nor SABAP1 describes the call. Grade B call from Mabusa, Mpumalanga. The filename is XC199337-2014-10-19 08_37 bush pipit.mp3. It was the only openly licensed recording above grade C.

research.note: No Newman page. Wikipedia and SABAP1 do not describe plumage or length, so those fields are empty. Population figures and the Kemp code RB were left unchanged. Status is resident: SABAP1 says the southeastern lowland race traylori seems essentially sedentary and birds were present all year in all parts of the range.
